stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

The applicant whom the panel interviewed on Monday has accepted the job offer.
hints: In "whom the panel interviewed", who did the interviewing, and who was interviewed?
Turn that part into a short sentence: "The panel interviewed ___." Would you put "he" or "him" in the blank?
If "him" fits, "whom" is right. If "he" fits, "who" is right. Then check that the main verb matches the main subject, "The applicant". If every part passes, choose "No error".

steps.action: Look at "whom the panel interviewed". The doer is "the panel". The applicant is the one who was interviewed.
Swap test: "The panel interviewed him." "Him" fits, so "whom" is correct.
steps.why: "Him" receives the action, and so does "whom". Both end in -m.

steps.action: Check "on Monday": "on" is the right word before a day. Correct.
Check "has accepted": the main subject is "The applicant", which is singular, so "has" is correct.
steps.why: "The panel" belongs to the describing part. It is not the subject of "has accepted".

steps.action: All parts are correct. The answer is "No error".

trapNotes.whom the panel interviewed: Many people use "who" for everything, so "whom" looks odd. But the panel did the interviewing and the applicant received it ("interviewed him"), so "whom" is correct.
trapNotes.on Monday: "On" is the right preposition for days of the week. This part is correct.
trapNotes.has accepted: "Have" might seem right if you match the verb with "the panel" or think of many people. But the subject is "The applicant", one person, so "has" is correct.
